metadata.title: Global Ocean Life & Marine Species Directory

species.habitat: Open Pelagic Waters and Polar Oceans
species.description: The blue whale is the largest known animal ever to have existed on Earth, consuming up to 4 metric tons of krill per day during feeding season.
species.primaryThreats: Ship strikes, commercial ocean noise, climate change affecting krill density, and marine plastic debris.

species.habitat: Tropical and Subtropical Coastal Waters & Coral Reefs

physicalAttributes.coloration: Olive-green to dark brown smooth carapace

species.description: Named for the greenish color of its subcutaneous fat, the green sea turtle migrates thousands of miles between foraging habitats and natal nesting beaches.
species.primaryThreats: Fisheries bycatch, coastal development destroying nesting grounds, boat strikes, and marine plastic ingestion.

physicalAttributes.coloration: Bright orange body with three distinct white vertical stripes

species.description: Possesses a mutualistic relationship with sea anemones; a protective mucus coating shields the fish from stinging nematocysts while providing territorial defense.
species.primaryThreats: Coral bleaching, destructive aquarium harvesting, and loss of sea anemone symbionts.

species.habitat: Tropical and Subtropical Pelagic Oceans & Offshore Seamounts
species.diet: Filter Feeder (Planktonic Crustaceans and Small Fish)

physicalAttributes.coloration: Dorsal jet black with chevron markings and pale ventral spots

species.description: Boasting the largest brain-to-body mass ratio of all cold-blooded fish, giant manta rays navigate open ocean currents with triangular pectoral fins spanning up to 7 meters.
species.primaryThreats: Targeted fishing for gill plates, entanglement in ghost gear, and microplastic ingestion.

species.habitat: Cool North Pacific Coastal Benthic Zones & Kelp Forests
species.description: The largest and longest-lived octopus species, possessing three hearts, blue hemocyanin copper-based blood, and remarkable cognitive problem-solving abilities.
species.primaryThreats: Water warming events, commercial trapping bycatch, ocean acidification, and benthic pollution.

species.habitat: Midnight and Twilight Bathypelagic Abyssal Depths

physicalAttributes.coloration: Pitch black to dark brown light-absorbing skin

species.description: Survives under thousands of pounds of hydrostatic pressure; female anglerfish wield a modified dorsal spine (illicium) tipped with a bioluminescent bacterial lure (esca) to attract prey.
species.primaryThreats: Deep-sea mineral mining, underwater noise disturbance, and microplastic contamination in the water column.

species.habitat: Coastal Inshore Waters, Bays, and Harbors
species.diet: Carnivore (Plankton, Mollusk Larvae, and Fish Eggs)

physicalAttributes.coloration: Translucent bell with four horseshoe-shaped gonads

species.description: Composed of over 95 percent water, moon jellies drift with tidal currents, using stinging cnidocytes on delicate marginal tentacles to sweep microplankton toward their oral arms.
species.primaryThreats: Plastic bag ingestion by marine predators mistaking jellies for food, temperature spikes, and chemical runoff.

species.diet: Apex Carnivore (Marine Mammals, Large Pelagic Fish, and Rays)

physicalAttributes.coloration: Dark slate gray dorsum with stark white countershading

species.description: Apex predator equipped with ampullae of Lorenzini electroreceptors capable of detecting microvolt bioelectric fields emitted by prey thousands of meters away.
species.primaryThreats: Commercial shark finning, gillnet entanglement, targeted trophy hunting, and habitat degradation.

species.habitat: Antarctic Pack Ice and Southern Ocean

physicalAttributes.coloration: Deep black plumage on back with bright golden auricular patches

species.description: The tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species, adapted with dense four-layered plumage, sub-dermal blubber, and the ability to dive deeper than 500 meters into sub-zero waters.
species.primaryThreats: Antarctic sea ice loss due to global heating, shifts in krill population, and extreme blizzard mortality.

species.habitat: Shallow Tropical Reef Crests and Fore-Reefs
species.diet: Symbiotic (Photosynthetic Zooxanthellae and Suspended Organic Particulates)

physicalAttributes.coloration: Golden tan to light olive with luminous pale growth tips

species.description: Keystone reef-building stony coral with intricate branching structures that resemble deer antlers, providing critical protective nursery habitats for hundreds of reef fish species.
species.primaryThreats: Ocean warming causing mass coral bleaching, ocean acidification, white band disease outbreaks, and agricultural sedimentation.
